rationale.idea: Replace same-validation checkpoint finalisation with a held-out user-split rule chosen from the epoch predictions of a single training run.
rationale.why_expected_to_help: The methodological risk is not the backbone but the selection procedure: choosing between best single epoch and checkpoint averaging on the exact validation users later used for reporting can overfit the finalisation rule. A user-held-out comparison tests whether any averaging rule generalises within the same run; if it does, we keep it, and if it does not, we fall back to the single epoch without spending another training pass.
rationale.grounded_in: Grounded in the recorded contested claim [2] that snapshot/top-N checkpoint ensembling was 'rejected by its own guard' because the comparison used validation to choose and score, plus the capability description of selection_rule_test: 'compares CHOOSING rules by selecting on one half of the validation users and scoring on the other'. Also grounded in the history where the same strong configuration scored 0.6042 with n_checkpoints=3, checkpoint_combine=True (node 0/3) versus 0.6038 with n_checkpoints=1, checkpoint_combine=False (node 4), a +0.0004 gap that is only 0.5 sigma and therefore unresolved by single-seed validation.

code_summary: The script trains one menu-equivalent configuration via train_lib.train_torch while recording per-epoch validation/test predictions. It then constructs candidate finalisation rules from the recorded checkpoints (best single epoch; average of top-2/top-3/top-5 validation epochs) and evaluates those rules with a user-held-out comparison: repeatedly split validation users into two halves, select the best rule on one half, score that chosen rule on the other half, and vice versa. The rule with the best cross-held-out mean primary is fixed, then used to produce the final full-validation metrics and blind test scores. Existing menu primitives can set n_checkpoints/checkpoint_combine, but cannot express 'choose the checkpoint combination rule by held-out user resampling inside the run' rather than by the same validation data that reports the result.
